questions.question: Which of the following items is NOT a part of the non-plan revenue expenditure of the government budget?

options.text: Central assistance for states and union territories

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central assistance for states and union territories.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Non-plan revenue expenditure:-**

 
 
• **It refers to the regular expenses incurred by the government in running its day-to-day operations and does not include any capital expenditures.**
 
• Salaries and pensions of government employees, subsidies to various sectors, and defense services are some of the major components of non-plan revenue expenditure. 
 
 
 
• **Central assistance:-**
 
 
• Central assistance for states and union territories, on the other hand, is a part of the plan expenditure, which refers to the government's spending on development and welfare schemes.
 
• Central assistance is provided to the states and union territories for specific purposes such as infrastructure development, poverty alleviation, and education.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Salaries and pensions: **

 
 
• This includes the salaries and pensions of government employees such as civil servants, police officers, and teachers.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies: **
 
 
• This refers to the financial assistance provided by the government to various sectors such as agriculture, industry, and exports, to promote their growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Defence services: **
 
 
• This includes the expenses incurred on the maintenance and modernization of the armed forces, as well as on border security and defense-related research and development.

questions.question:
Which of the following is an objective of the Government Budget?

A) GDP Growth

B) Reallocation of Resources

C) Balanced Regional Growth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All- A, B and C.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reallocation of resources:-**

 
 
• It refers to the government's ability to distribute resources in a way that benefits the economy and society as a whole.
 
• Reallocation of resources is also an important objective as it allows the government to allocate resources to areas that need it the most, such as education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Balanced regional growth:-**
 
 
• It refers to the government's efforts to ensure that economic growth is distributed evenly across all regions of the country.
 
• Balanced regional growth is important as it ensures that economic growth is distributed evenly across all regions of the country, reducing regional disparities and promoting overall economic development. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP growth:-**

 
 
• It is an important objective of the government budget as it reflects the overall health of the economy and its ability to create jobs and improve the standard of living for citizens.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the functions of the Government budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Redistribution of income and wealth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Redistribution of income and wealth: **

 
 
• This is one of the primary functions of the government budget.
 
• It involves the allocation of resources and funds to promote social and economic equity.
 
• The government can achieve this through progressive taxation, welfare programs, and subsidies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Management of money supply:**

 
 
• This refers to the control and regulation of money supply in the economy.
 
• The government can adjust the money supply through various tools like open market operations, reserve requirements, and discount rates.
 
• This helps in maintaining stable economic growth and controlling inflation.
 
 
 
• **Maintaining strict budgetary balance: **
 
 
• This refers to the practice of keeping government spending in line with revenue generated.
 
• A strict budgetary balance is important to avoid a fiscal deficit, which can lead to inflation and a decrease in the value of the currency.
 
 
 
• **Price fixation: **
 
 
• This refers to the government's role in regulating the prices of goods and services in the economy.
 
• The government can control prices through price ceilings or price floors. However, this is not a primary function of the government budget.

questions.question: What is the name of the scheme aimed at conservation of wetlands, which was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrit Dharohar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amrit Dharohar** is the name of the scheme aimed at the conservation of wetlands, which was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24.
 
• The scheme is designed to enhance the protection and management of wetlands across India.
 
• Wetlands are crucial ecosystems that support a wide range of biodiversity and provide numerous environmental benefits such as water filtration, flood control, and carbon sequestration.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's broader efforts to promote sustainable development and environmental conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil all year or for varying periods during the year, including during the growing season.
 
• India is a signatory to the Ramsar Convention, an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands.
 
• The Ramsar Convention aims to halt the worldwide loss of wetlands and to conserve, through wise use and management, those that remain.
 
• India has 94 Ramsar sites, covering an area of over 1.3 million hectares.
 
• Conserving wetlands can also help in achieving several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including those related to water, climate action, and life on land.

questions.question: The stabilisation function of the government budget mainly includes.

options.text: intervention to expand or reduce the demand
distribution of income in society in a fair way

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** intervention to expand or reduce the demand.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stabilisation function:-**

 
 
• It is aimed at maintaining economic stability by adjusting the level of aggregate demand in the economy.
 
• The stabilization function of the government budget is a macroeconomic concept that deals with the management of the overall level of economic activity in the economy. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal policy tools:-**

 
 
• These are used by the government to influence the level of aggregate demand in the economy. Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing government spending, reducing taxes, and increasing borrowing to stimulate economic growth. In contrast, contractionary fiscal policy involves reducing government spending, increasing taxes, and reducing borrowing to slow down economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Allocation of resources:- **
 
 
• It is an important function of the government, which involves the distribution of resources among different sectors of the economy to achieve economic efficiency and equity.
 
 
 
• **Production of public goods:-**
 
 
• It is another important function of the government, which involves the provision of goods and services that are not provided by the private sector, such as national defense, public health, and education.
 
 
 
• **Distribution of income in society:-**
 
 
• It is an important issue that involves the fair distribution of income among different groups in the economy. The government can use taxation and social welfare programs to achieve a fair distribution of income.

questions.question: SLR is an important tool used by RBI to control money supply in the economy. The full form of SLR is_______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Statutory Liquidity Ratio.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The SLR is fixed by **the RBI**. CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR have been the traditional tools of the central bank's monetary policy to control credit growth, the flow of liquidity, and inflation in the economy.
 
• The SLR was prescribed by Section 24 (2A) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
 
• **During inflation, RBI raises SLR to control the bank credit**.
 
• SLR is a monetary policy tool that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) uses **to assess the liquidity at the banks' disposal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reserve Bank of India is the authority to control inflation through **monetary policies** which it does by increasing: 

 
 
• Bank rates, 
 
• Repo rates, 
 
• Cash reserve ratio, 
 
• Buying dollars, 
 
• Regulating money supply 
 
• Availability of credit.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best estimate of the total borrowings by the government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Deficit.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **A fiscal deficit **represents the difference between the **government's total expenditure** and its **total revenue**.
 
• It is a key indicator of the **government's borrowings** and reflects the extent to which it is relying on debt to fund its spending.
 
• **Primary deficit** is a narrower measure that **excludes interest payments** on past borrowings.
 
• It indicates the government's borrowing needs for **current spending** but does not capture the burden of past debt.
 
• **Revenue receipts **represent the government's income from** taxes, fees, and other sources.** 
 
• **Money supply** is a measure of the total amount of** money in circulation** in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue receipts **can be further classified into **tax revenue and non-tax revenue.**
 
• Tax revenue is the income from taxes such as **income tax, corporate tax, GST, etc.**
 
• Non-tax revenue is the income from other sources such as** dividends from public sector enterprises, interest receipts, etc.**
 
• **Money supply **can be measured in different ways, such as** M1, M2, and M3**.
 
• M1 includes currency in** circulation, demand deposits,** and other liquid assets.
 
• M2 includes **M1 plus savings deposits, time deposits,** and other less liquid assets.
 
• M3 includes **M2 plus large time deposits and institutional money market funds.**

questions.question: ________ is defined as excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings during a fiscal year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal deficit.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is the difference between a government's total expenditure and its total revenue, excluding any borrowing, within a specific fiscal year.
 
• **Formula**
 
 
• Fiscal Deficit=**Total Expenditure−(Total Revenue+Non-Debt Receipts)**
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Economy**:
 
 
• **Inflation**: Persistent fiscal deficits can lead to higher inflation if funded by printing more money.
 
• **Interest Rates**: Higher fiscal deficits can lead to increased borrowing costs as the government competes for funds in the financial markets.
 
• **Public Debt**: A high fiscal deficit adds to the government’s debt burden, potentially leading to higher interest payments in the future.
 
 
 
• **Policy Measures**
 
 
• **Increase Revenue**: Through higher taxes or better tax compliance.
 
• **Reduce Expenditure**: By cutting down on non-essential spending.
 
• **Borrow Responsibly**: Managing debt to ensure it does not become unsustainable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Type of Deficit
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Income Deficit
 The shortfall between total government revenue and total government expenditure.
 
 

 Structural Deficit
 The part of the fiscal deficit that arises from structural imbalances in the economy and budgetary policies.
 
 

 Gross Primary Deficit
 The fiscal deficit before accounting for interest payments on previous borrowings.

questions.question: Which of the following measures can be adopted by the government to reduce revenue deficit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax reforms**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tax reforms** are crucial measures that can help the government reduce revenue deficits.
 
• By implementing effective tax reforms, the government can increase its revenue without necessarily increasing tax rates.
 
• Tax reforms can include broadening the tax base, improving tax compliance, and reducing tax evasion.
 
• Improved tax administration and the introduction of modern technology in tax collection processes can also contribute significantly to reducing revenue deficits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Offering freebies and increasing subsidies may lead to higher government expenditure, potentially worsening the revenue deficit.
 
• Increasing money supply can lead to inflationary pressures and is not a sustainable solution for revenue deficits.
 
• Effective tax reforms can make the tax system more efficient and equitable, thus boosting government revenue without imposing undue burdens on taxpayers.
 
• Governments around the world have successfully reduced revenue deficits through comprehensive tax reforms.

questions.question: A government budget is an annual financial statement which outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year. Depending on the feasibility of these estimates which of the following is **NOT** the budget type?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Economy budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Among the options, only an **Economy budget**__ is **NOT** a budget type.
 
• A government budget is an annual financial statement that outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year.
 
• In India, it is a constitutional requirement (**Article 112**) that the government give a statement of estimated income and expenditures to Parliament for each financial year that runs from April 1 to March 31.
 
• This 'Annual Financial Statement' is the government's primary budget document.
 
• Budgets are grouped into three categories based on these estimates:
 
 
• Balanced budget.
 
• Surplus budget.
 
• Deficit budget.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A government budget is said to be a **balanced budget** if the estimated government expenditures in a given fiscal year are equal to the expected government receipts.

 
 
• A balanced budget ensures economic stability if implemented successfully.
 
• A balanced budget is Inapplicable in less developed countries as it limits the scope of economic growth.
 
 
 
• A government budget is said to be a** surplus budget **if the expected government revenues exceed the estimated government expenditure in a particular financial year.
 
 
• A country's financial wealth is indicated by a surplus budget.
 
 
 
• If the estimated government expenditure exceeds the expected government revenue in a given fiscal year, the budget is considered to be a **deficit budget.**
 
 
• A deficit budget is best suited for developing economies, such as India

questions.question: What was the estimation for the ﬁscal deﬁcit in the ﬁnancial year 2019-20 ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.3% of GDP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **3.3% of GDP was the estimation for the ﬁscal deﬁcit in the ﬁnancial year 2019-20**__.
 
• **Fiscal deficit** is the difference between income and expenditure of the Government.
 __
 
• **One of the key sources to bridge the deficit is borrowing.**
 
 
 
• Reasons for the higher deficit include a fall in nominal GDP growth rate to 7.2 percent and a decline in not only tax but also non-tax revenue.
 
• As a result, the fiscal deficit was over ₹9.35-lakh crore against the revised Budget estimate of ₹7.66-lakh crore.
 
• A higher deficit also reflects much lower revenue from disinvestment and spectrum.
 
• At the same time cut in corporate tax, mid-year has an impact of over ₹1.45 lakh crore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **​Fiscal Deficit =** Total expenditure of the government (capital and revenue expenditure) – Total income of the government (Revenue receipts + recovery of loans + other receipts).

 
 
• **Expenditure component**: The government in its Budget allocates funds for several works, including payments of salaries, pensions, etc. (revenue expenditure) and creation of assets such as infrastructure, development, etc. (capital expenditure).
 
• **Income component: **The income component is made of two variables, revenue generated from taxes levied by the Centre and the income generated from non-tax variables.
 
 
• The taxable income consists of the amount generated from corporation tax, income tax, customs duties, excise duties, GST, among others.
 
• Meanwhile, the non-taxable income comes from external grants, interest receipts, dividends and profits, receipts from Union Territories, among others.
 
 
 
 
 
• **It is different from revenue deficit which is only related to revenue expenditure and revenue receipts of the government.**
 
• The government meets the fiscal deficit by borrowing money.
 
 
• In a way, the total borrowing requirements of the government in a financial year are equal to the fiscal deficit in that year.
 
 
 
• A high fiscal deficit can also be good for the economy if the money spent goes into the creation of productive assets like highways, roads, ports, and airports that boost economic growth and result in job creation.
 
• **The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 provides that the Centre should take appropriate measures to limit the fiscal deficit up to 3% of the GDP by 31st March 2021.**

questions.question: What is a revenue deficit in the government budget?

options.text: The excess of expenditure over revenue, excluding interest payments on debt
The excess of revenue over expenditure, excluding interest payments on debt
The excess of revenue over expenditure, including interest payments on debt
The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt** is known as a revenue deficit in the government budget.
 
• A revenue deficit indicates that the government's revenue receipts are not sufficient to meet its revenue expenditure.
 
• This type of deficit is a key indicator of the financial health of the government and reflects its ability to manage its finances.
 
• A persistent revenue deficit can lead to higher borrowings and increased debt burden for the government.
 
• Reducing the revenue deficit is crucial for maintaining fiscal discipline and ensuring long-term economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue receipts** include tax revenues (like income tax, corporate tax, GST) and non-tax revenues (like interest receipts, dividends, and profits from public sector enterprises).
 
• **Revenue expenditure** includes expenses incurred for the normal functioning of government departments and various services, interest payments on debt, and subsidies.
 
• Unlike capital expenditure, revenue expenditure does not result in the creation of assets or reduction in liabilities.
 
• Efforts to reduce revenue deficit may include enhancing revenue receipts through better tax compliance and administration, and rationalizing expenditure.
 
• The government may also implement structural reforms to improve the efficiency and productivity of public sector enterprises.
